const r1 = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: `GOAL: scope-gate all four proposals against the 5-point contract and read each frozen bundle.
READ: proposal texts (CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN, CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN-RQ, CURVCHART-RESGUARD, CURVEBEND-NORM-RESIDUAL) and bundles 9637a2495b60c669 / 634a0d7731a5d022 / dfec9cb5b35ea444 / 6476469bc16f6590 (E1-E13 each; E4-E11 identical across bundles).
OBSERVED: all four name a train-only behaviour signal (directed transitions / successor sets / Ollivier curvature), an explicit curved op (Poincare distance, exp/log, Mobius add), a single connected pathway, the three switches, and a one-run testable effect -> all four are IN SCOPE, so the ranking is on merit, not admissibility.
Key shared evidence: prior curvature-on-radius arm collapsed to 2/13/56 SIDs, collision 0.998, L1 hit 0.982/0.980, recall 0.041888 vs 0.055537 frozen. E6 shows the mechanism of the loss: for l1_br, target SID absent from the 20 beams in 53546/57439 rows (0.932) and recall 0.04671, whereas tables with heavy support (l1_br_euclid 0.0847 in-beam, 0.06207; l1_only 0.0855/0.06233; resample 0.0884/0.06363) recover 0.062-0.064. So SID cardinality / in-beam survival, not token NLL, is the recall gate (E6 vs E7; resample has T1 NLL 4.55 yet the best recall).
E8 says the natural coarse partition is strongly imbalanced (share-one-cluster K=16 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822; neg 0.1352 vs 0.0129) and that a small K keeps behavioural neighbours together, which is what width-20 prefix survival needs. E9 says successor-cohort signal is real (0.9291 vs 0.8871, profile overlap beats all ten negatives in 0.5898 of pairs). E11 says the existing first prefix is only weakly behavioural (0.0907 vs 0.067 permuted).
OPEN: convert these into a total order; no run, so rank expected one-run value.`});

const r2 = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: `GOAL: compare the four mechanisms on (a) whether they can repeat the documented collapse, (b) whether the behaviour actually changes the core computation, (c) whether one run can make the case.
OBSERVED / REASONING:
1) CURVCHART-RESGUARD: code vectors, norm, count, radius and EMA are byte-identical to the inherited baseline; the only change is a per-codeword chart distance inside the assignment softmax, with g_e=exp(-s_e/2) from standardised item-level Ollivier curvature and a clip to [0.5,2]x the neutral q0. This is the only proposal whose resolution-protecting object (the codebook) is provably not a function of curvature, and it uses the richer 24556-node item-level curvature that bundles E1/E2 describe, rather than a 3-vector. Risk is a no-op (<0.5% assignment change), which the proposal itself makes the disconfirming observation. Matches E5/E9 evidence that successor-side curvature separates items.
2) CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN: resolution intent is right and the successor-community coupling (a_ik, c_ik=c_l*exp(-a_ik)) is grounded in E9. But the stated guarantee ("per-level usage multiset exactly the Euclidean one") is not delivered by the stated readout: the plan is Sinkhorn with column sums u_k and the code is argmax_k P_ik, and row-wise argmax of an entropic plan does not reproduce column marginals. So the structural claim is an aspiration, not a guarantee, and "code's community" is left undefined. Highest chance of being a <1% no-op because capacity anchoring forces the plan toward the Euclidean solution.
3) CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN-RQ: maximal resolution attempt (uniform B/K columns) but E8 shows the corpus is genuinely imbalanced; forcing ~4 items/code/step at 256 level-1 codes splits behavioural neighbours, which E8 identifies as exactly what width-20 prefix survival depends on. Same argmax-vs-marginal inconsistency, plus oscillatory one-epoch-lag feedback and 8-shuffle null cost. Its own risk list concedes level-1 may lose the dominant generic prefix.
4) CURVEBEND-NORM-RESIDUAL: norm-preserving direction bend on levels 2-3 only; internally consistent and cheap, but codebook is untouched only because nothing is constrained, it leaves the level-1/usage pathology untouched, and a unit-direction bend in d=64 is the most likely of the four to be numerically negligible; its evidence hook is the same Spearman -0.20 profile that was already spent (unsuccessfully) on the radius.
OPEN: final order and one-line evidence-grounded reasons.`});

const r3 = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: `GOAL: deliver the final total order (positions 1..4, no ties, every idea once).
DECISION (answer):
RANK: CURVCHART-RESGUARD | position=1 | reason=only proposal whose code table, norm, count and radius are provably unchanged, while the assignment spends a per-codeword chart built from the item-level standardised curvature that E1/E2/E5 measure and E5/E9 show carries successor signal; it targets the documented failure (radius spend -> 2/13/56, 0.041888) without changing resolution and states a one-run disconfirmer (<0.5% assignment change).
RANK: CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN | position=2 | reason=behaviour (successor fraction a_ik across E9's 0.9291-vs-0.8871 cohort signal) genuinely enters the cost and the capacity anchor is aimed at E6's in-beam/SID-cardinality gate, but the claimed exact-Euclidean usage multiset is not implied by row-wise argmax of a column-constrained Sinkhorn plan, "code community" is undefined, and anchoring to Euclidean counts risks the <1% no-op its own risk list names.
RANK: CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN-RQ | position=3 | reason=uniform B/K columns maximise used codes but E8 measures a strongly imbalanced corpus (K=16 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822; negatives 0.1352 vs 0.0129) and states that small-K behavioural co-location is what width-20 prefix survival needs, so mandatory equipartition plausibly costs the prefix sharing that E6 ties to recall; same argmax/marginal inconsistency plus lagged-feedback oscillation.
RANK: CURVEBEND-NORM-RESIDUAL | position=4 | reason=norm-preserving direction-only bend on levels 2-3 leaves the level-1 usage pathology of E6 untouched (l1_br 0.932 SID-absent-from-beams) and is the most likely to be negligible at d=64; its only evidence hook is the Spearman -0.20 profile that the failed radius arm already tried to spend, and E6/E7 locate the recall gate in SID survival, not residual direction.
Every proposal appears exactly once; positions are 1,2,3,4 with no gaps.`});
return [r1, r2, r3].map(x => typeof x === 'string' ? x : JSON.stringify(x));
